text.p: French aluminium and packaging group Pechiney said on Thursday that it remained cautious about 1997, after announcing a downturn to net loss in 1996.
It also reiterated its declaration of February 17 that the positive impact of a stronger dollar and improved aluminium demand, if they continued, would be felt only several months into 1997.

"Since the start of the year, there have been a number of encouraging signs, especially in world demand for aluminium and semi-finished aluminium products, and also a marked appreciation of the dollar," it said.
"Nevertheless, and if they hold true, these factors will only have an impact after the first months of 1997," it said.

"The considerable destocking movement of 1996 as well as the maintaining of a freeze on sizeable Western aluminium production capacity commit the group to a cautious view as far as the outlook for activity in 1997 is concerned."
Pechiney was commenting in a results statement after announcing a 1996 net attributable loss of 2.977 billion francs after a profit of 1.465 billion francs in 1995.
